cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend, because we're hitting the road with Jesus and His disciples. The day of His ascension is getting close. And Jesus sets out with His mind made up.

cards.question: As the day of His ascension approaches, Jesus resolutely sets out for ___.

cards.text: Jesus sends messengers on ahead into a village of the Samaritans to make arrangements for Him. That's an advance team, friend, while the rest of us just pull into the driveway and text "outside" like that's a whole PLAN.

cards.question: Jesus' messengers reach the Samaritan village. How do the people there respond to Him?
True or false: The Samaritan village refuses to welcome Jesus because He is heading for Jerusalem.

cards.text: James and John, two of Jesus' disciples, see all this. And they come to Jesus with an offer that is, uh… a LOT.

cards.question: James and John ask Jesus if He wants them to call down ___ from heaven to consume the people of that Samaritan village.
True or false: When James and John offer to call down fire from heaven on the Samaritan village, Jesus tells them to go ahead.

cards.text: So Jesus and His disciples just go on to another village. A whole village turns Him away and He keeps walking, while one cookie sticks to MY tray and I need to sit down a minute.
As they're walking along the road, someone says to Jesus, “I will follow You wherever You go.” WHEREVER. That is a big word, friend.

cards.question: Jesus answers the man who says he'll follow Him wherever: “Foxes have dens and birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has no place to lay His head.” What is Jesus warning him about?

answers.text: Following Him means no settled home
The road ahead has wild animals
The man needs a house first

cards.text: A little farther down the road, Jesus turns to another man.

cards.question: True or false: On the road, Jesus says to another man, “Follow Me.”

cards.text: The man replies, “Lord, first let me go and bury my father.” And Jesus answers with a line I bet stopped everybody on that road: “Let the dead bury their own dead.”

cards.question: Instead of burying his father first, Jesus tells this man to go and ___ the kingdom of God.

cards.text: Then still another man speaks up: “I will follow You, Lord; but first…” There's that word AGAIN.

cards.question: True or false: This third man asks Jesus to let him first say farewell to his family.

cards.text: Jesus answers him with a picture from the field: a man who puts his hand to the plow. Friend, the only thing I've ever pushed is dough, and even THAT gets away from me.

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, what does the man at the plow do that makes him not fit for the kingdom of God?

findings.problem: Discovery questions dominate the stop. Cards 2, 4, 5, 8, 13, 15 and 17 ask for unseen destinations, responses, reasons or wording that cannot be inferred from the earlier cards. Only cards 7, 11 and 19 give the baker a reasonable basis for an informed pick, so most choices depend on luck rather than reasoning.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Jerusalem has not appeared in any earlier card, and nothing in the setup lets the baker infer that destination rather than Nazareth or Capernaum. The blank therefore tests an unseen word instead of meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The walkthrough never tells the baker that Jesus turned and rebuked James and John in Luke 9:55. Marking the statement that Jesus told them to go ahead as false only establishes what He did not do, leaving an important detail of the passage untold.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentence units: the setup containing the quotation, the one-word sentence "WHEREVER." and "That is a big word, friend."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The earlier cards never mention proclaiming the kingdom, and the setup gives no basis for choosing "proclaim" over "inherit" or "await." The baker must guess the unseen wording of Jesus' command.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
